comments.author: Houshalter
comments.why_zh: 利用内存访问暴力通关 NES 游戏的通用玩法。
comments.quote_zh: 这里有一个例子，一个人做了一个通用游戏博弈算法，靠暴力破解的方式通关任何 NES 游戏
comments.text_zh: 为什么不使用游戏模拟器呢？用流行的 NES 模拟器，你可以逐帧推进游戏。你可以读取与分数对应的原始内存地址。你可以随时转储内存，并把游戏重新加载到某个特定游戏状态。你甚至可以通过摆弄游戏内存，用许多有趣的方式操纵游戏。或者，如果你愿意，也可以让 AI 算法访问内存地址，将其作为额外信息，而不是依赖纯粹的机器视觉。这里有一个例子，一个人做了一个通用游戏博弈算法，靠暴力破解的方式通关任何 NES 游戏：[VIDEO] 从 AI 的角度看，这未必有趣——这个游玩算法只是暴力破解。但它展示了利用这个平台可以做到什么：轻松重载到之前的状态，并探索反事实的未来（这正是 RL 算法会做的事情）。他还有一个很酷的算法，通过观察人类游玩并查看哪些内存地址在递增，来找出任意游戏的目标函数。这比编写 OCR 代码从屏幕上读取分数和游戏结束状态要容易使用得多。
comments.text: Why not use game emulators? With popular NES emulators you can advance the game frame by frame. You can read the raw memory addresses that correspond to the score. You can dump the memory at any time and reload the game to a specific game state. You can even manipulate the games in many fun ways by messing around with the game memory. Or give an AI algorithm access to memory addresses as additional information, instead of relying on pure machine vision, if you want to do that.. Here's an example of a guy who made a general game playing algorithm that brute forces it's way through any NES game: [VIDEO] This isn't necessarily interesting from an AI perspective - the playing algorithm is just brute force. But it shows what can be done with the platform, easily reloading to previous states and exploring counterfactual futures (which is exactly the sort of thing RL algorithms do.) He also has a cool algorithm for finding the objective function of an arbitrary game, by watching a human play, and seeing what memory addresses increment. Which is a lot more easy to use than writing OCR code to read the score and game over states from the screen.

comments.author: MrPoush
comments.why_zh: 解释了 LearnFun 如何找到内存中的分数和生命数字节。
comments.text_zh: Tom7 用他的 Learnfun 和 Playfun 实现了其中一部分（[VIDEO]）——它会寻找内存中字节的字典序变化（也就是说，某个字节似乎几乎总是在增加，而当它突然减小时，相邻的一个字节会增加），以此来计算那些递增数值（分数、x 坐标）所在的内存位置；类似地，它也会检测通常似乎在减小的字节（生命数）。然后它尝试玩游戏，选择能让应该增加的数值增加的输入（向右移动、获得生命），或者尽量不让那些在减小的数值减少（别死掉）。
comments.text: Tom7 implemented some of this with his Learnfun and Playfun ( [VIDEO] ) - It looks for lexicographical changes to bytes in memory (i.e., one byte seems to almost always increase, and then when it suddenly decrements, a neighboring byte is incremented) as a way of calculating memory location for increasing values (score, x-position), and similarly detects bytes that generally seem to decrease (lives). It then tries to play the game, choosing inputs that increase the values that should be increasing (move right, gain lives), or tries not to decrease the values that are decreasing (don't die).
